default_outpost.doc: Where a character is put when its row names neither a map nor a last outpost - a row written before character creation filled one in. 148 is Ascalon City (pre-Searing), the base game's starting outpost and already in the map catalogue. The outpost a character enters is otherwise written by character creation, by a scripted event and by travelling, so this is only ever the fallback. A stand-in for a campaign whose own starting outpost this tree has not measured (docs/22-world-model.md).

map_type_main_town.doc: The client's MapType value for a town or outpost. A destination of this kind is never substituted: the client asked for a place and is in it. This number is the CLIENT'S - it reads it out of the map catalogue and out of the request it sends - so changing it here changes what this server believes, not what the client does.

map_type_main_explorable.doc: The client's MapType value for an explorable area. Entering one from outside is replaced by the last outpost the character stood in, because the game puts a character in an outpost, not in the middle of a field. The client's number, as above.

map_type_character_creation.doc: The client's MapType value for the character-creation instance: the one destination that is a conversation rather than a place. The client asks for it by this type beside the creation map id. The client's number, as above.

creation_map.doc: The map id of the character-creation instance: the one destination that is a conversation rather than a place. The client asks for it by this id beside map type 11, and it is the value a character row carries when nothing has been written yet, so it must be the same number the catalogue and the rows use for 'no map'. A file that changed it without changing those would make every unplaced character look placed.
